core_obligations: Show that (2) implies (1): given a relation among the monomials x^E with coefficients in kK^p, apply the dual derivations theta_i to obtain relations of strictly smaller total degree, contradicting the choice of a minimal relation (proof lines 11380-11393).

Show that (a) implies (b): if the x_i form a p-basis then K is presented as kK^p[X_i]/(X_i^p - x_i^p), from which the differentials dx_i are a K-basis of the differential module (proof lines 11394-11398).

Use Zorn's lemma to extend any p-independent collection to a maximal one, and show that a maximal p-independent set is a p-basis: if x lies outside the subfield generated by kK^p and the x_i then x^p lies in that subfield and x may be adjoined, contradicting maximality (proof lines 11400-11408).

Deduce (b) implies (a) by combining the equivalence of (1) and (2) with the previous step, so a set whose differentials form a basis is a maximal p-independent set and hence a p-basis (proof lines 11410-11415).
proof_roadmap: Interval comparison against the 57 public records of more-algebra.tex: no recorded interval covers 11362-11415. The nearest records are 345 (11457-11518, tag 07P4, filtered subfield intersections and characteristic-p differentials) and 346 (11859-11910, tag 07PH, a derivation detecting a non-pth-power in a finite-type domain); both belong to the same characteristic-p block of the chapter and use the vocabulary of this lemma, but both prove different statements and start after this card's interval ends.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the main structure theorem for a field extension K over a field k of characteristic p: p-independence of a subset is equivalent to linear independence of its differentials in the module of Kaehler differentials, every p-independent collection extends to a p-basis and p-bases exist, and a subset is a p-basis exactly when its differentials form a K-basis of the differential module (statement lines 11362-11377). The proof is a 36-line argument of four independent parts (proof lines 11380-11415): (2) implies (1) by applying the derivations theta_i dual to the x_j to a minimal relation and producing a relation of strictly smaller total degree, which is a contradiction; (a) implies (b) by presenting K as kK^p[X_i]/(X_i^p - x_i^p) and reading off the differentials; p-independence extends to a maximal p-independent set by Zorn's lemma, and a maximal p-independent set is shown to be a p-basis by adjoining a hypothetical element outside the subfield generated by kK^p and the x_i and contradicting maximality; finally (b) implies (a) closes the circle using the equivalence already proved. The two places where the reader has to bring in background are the existence of the derivations theta_i and the presentation of K over kK^p, both of which are standard for fields of characteristic p and neither of which is proved here.
